cases.question: when did the brackwater canal open
cases.passage: The Brackwater Canal is a broad canal in the county of Lisle, linking the town of Orringham with the tidal River Brack. It was promoted by a group of coal merchants led by Hester Callow and surveyed in 1791. The canal opened to traffic in 1798, after a long delay at the Fenby flight of locks. Commercial carrying ended in 1961, and the waterway was restored for pleasure boats in 1994.

cases.question: who is the current chief executive of harlow sound ferries

In 2019 it was bought by the Westerly Transport Group.

cases.question: what is the velling cut
cases.passage: The Velling Cut is a short navigable canal that bypasses a loop of the River Ostley near the market town of Velling. It is just over two kilometres long and has a single lock at its southern end. The cut was dug in 1774 to save barges a journey of nine kilometres around the loop. It is now managed by the Ostley Navigation Trust.

cases.question: how long is the hendry tunnel

cases.question: which airline is the biggest at corriemoor airport

The largest operator at the airport is Highland Skyways, which flies to eleven destinations from a base there. Other airlines, including Fennick Air, run seasonal flights to the coast. cases.question: how many passengers does westfold airport handle a year

The airport was opened in 1962 by the Westfold Borough Council, which still owns a majority stake. Its busiest route is the service to the island of Carrisk, flown up to nine times a day.

cases.question: where is lanmore station

cases.question: who operates trains on the felbrook branch

It is twelve kilometres long and has three intermediate stations.

cases.question: who runs the kilmarten ferry today
cases.passage: The Kilmarten Ferry is a passenger ferry across the mouth of the River Lune Dhu between Kilmarten and Ardlish. A crossing has been recorded at this point since the fourteenth century. From 1902 until 1977 the ferry was run by the Ardlish Estate, which built the stone slipways still in use. The present boat, the Morag Bell, was launched in 2011 and carries up to forty passengers.

cases.question: when was the dunsford bypass opened
cases.passage: The Dunsford Bypass is a single carriageway road that takes through traffic around the east side of the market town of Dunsford. It is 6.4 kilometres long and has four roundabouts. The scheme was first proposed in 1971, but objections over the crossing of Dunsford Marsh held it up for two decades. Construction began in 1996 and the road was opened to traffic in 1999. A cycle path was added along its length in 2015.

cases.question: how many locks are on the tarrant navigation
cases.passage: The Tarrant Navigation is a river navigation that makes the River Tarrant passable for boats from Selby Haven to the town of Coldharbour. There are seventeen locks on the navigation, most of them built of local sandstone. Improvement works were authorised by an act of 1740 and completed in 1756. The navigation is 41 kilometres long and rises 52 metres from the tidal river.

cases.question: what is the orwen funicular

cases.question: who designed hallam cross station

cases.question: how many platforms does larch road station have

The station has four platforms, two of which are used only by peak-hour trains. It opened in 1889 and was renamed from Westley Halt in 1932.

cases.question: when did the ravensholme tramway close

The first horse-drawn trams ran in 1884, and the system was electrified in 1902. At its largest the network had 23 kilometres of route and 48 cars.

cases.question: what does the cardle valley railway connect

cases.question: how long does the ferry from ballintra to skerrin take

cases.question: who built the halcombe incline

cases.question: speed limit on the mardale expressway

The speed limit along most of its length is 100 kilometres per hour, reduced to 70 near the airport junction. It opened in 2004 and is 18 kilometres long. The road was built by Strand Civil under a contract worth 310 million crowns.

cases.question: who is the managing director of lessingham airport

The airport's first managing director was Clara Doyle, who led it through its expansion in the 1970s. It is owned by the Lessingham Regional Authority and handled 1.2 million passengers in 2023.
cases.looking_for: the name of the current managing director

cases.question: how many passengers does brenna bay airport handle

In 2023 it handled 2.8 million passengers, most of them on summer charter flights. The runway was lengthened to 2,600 metres in 1997 to take larger jets. The airport is run by the island government through the Brenna Airports Company.

cases.question: what company runs the ferry to the isle of tarne

It was formed in 1971 by the merger of the Ollach Steam Packet and the Tarne Motor Boat Company. Its fleet consists of three ships, the largest of which is the Tarne Venturer. cases.question: what gauge is the skelwith quarry railway

cases.question: who was the engineer of the grindle canal

It was authorised by an act of 1792 and fully opened in 1801. The company's chairman was the landowner Lord Ashcote, who held a third of the shares. cases.question: when did the weyburn line reopen

cases.question: when did the cleat ferry service start

A new slipway was built at Cleat in 1974, and a larger ship, the Dunmore Lass, arrived in 1975. Around 90,000 passengers use the ferry each year.

cases.question: how long is the runway at felling moss airport

The airport has one paved runway, 1,350 metres long, and a grass strip used by gliders. Its operator, Felling Aviation, also runs a flying school with twelve aircraft.

cases.question: how many people use crossmere station

cases.question: when did the last cargo boat use the thurlow canal
cases.passage: The Thurlow Canal is a narrow canal linking the River Thurl with the town of Kessington. It was opened in 1794 and carried coal, grain and bricks. Traffic fell after a railway was built alongside it in 1852. The last cargo boat to use the canal was the Hopeful, which carried coal to Kessington in 1938. The canal was restored for pleasure boats in the 1990s.

cases.question: what is the record number of passengers at ardmoor airport
cases.passage: Ardmoor Airport is an international airport serving the city of Ardmoor and the western hills. In 2023 it handled 3.4 million passengers, an increase of nine per cent on the year before. The airport has one runway and a terminal extended in 2015. cases.question: how long is the lanyon tramway
